tasks.short: Prepare, copy, scan, send and store documents using office equipment.

steps.what: Retrieve electronic documents and stage them for printing or scanning.
Prepare paper, remove staples and load the scanner or copier.
Select settings and run the scanner or copier.
Check page count, legibility, orientation and completeness.
Address and send the checked document by email or fax.
Name and file the electronic copy with its delivery receipt.

tasks.design: Submit electronic originals directly from the {DOCS} or {EMAIL}, removing print-and-rescan detours. Configure scanner and copier presets in the {OTHER} office-equipment interface; a small {WORKFLOW} checks files, prepares delivery and stores receipts in the {DOCS}. The clerk handles paper, checks uncertain scans and approves external recipients.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper handling remained physical. Device settings, destinations and filing conventions differed between teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scan profiles and document routing handle much of this. AI-assisted coding makes small file checks and connectors cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile originals, bound documents, jams and missing pages still need physical attention. Older devices may lack supported interfaces.
tasks.human_edge: Notice missing pages, protect originals and recognise when an apparently readable copy is unusable.

ambition.what: Accessible digital document packs for colleagues who struggle with paper.

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer file transfers and more support for difficult documents. The clerk can choose accessible formats within agreed standards; release authority stays the same.

reach.task: Prepare searchable, correctly indexed document packs.
reach.learn: Document metadata, accessibility checks and retention schedules.

evidence.claim: Business post scanning and conversion of forms into data are available today.
Presets, file validation and routing can reduce clerical handling without a model loop.

assumptions: This models a common document-handling cycle, rather than every use of a personal computer.
The {OTHER} category covers scanner, copier and fax interfaces.
Electronic originals are available for some requests.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Which devices support presets, direct storage and delivery receipts?
Which requests require physical copies or original documents?
What access, retention and recipient restrictions apply?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed changes?
research_questions: Which print-and-rescan paths can disappear entirely?
Can page-count and image-quality checks catch the team's common failures?
new_work: Review flagged scans and delivery failures.
Maintain destination lists, presets and filing rules.
Test device changes and access permissions.
Apply GDPR controls to stored documents and assess any added AI use under the EU AI Act.

tasks.short: Answer calls, find the right recipient, transfer callers and pass on messages.

steps.what: Greet the caller and establish their purpose.
Look up the department, contact details and availability.
Choose a recipient or decide to take a message.
Transfer the caller and check that the connection succeeds.
Record and confirm the caller's name, number, message and urgency when needed.
Send the confirmed message to the recipient.

tasks.design: Configure a searchable contact directory, routing buttons and failed-transfer fallback in the {TELEPHONY}, using permitted availability from the {CALENDAR}. A structured message form in the {WORKFLOW} sends confirmed messages through the {EMAIL} or {CHAT}; callers can still reach the clerk directly.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directories were stale and availability was scattered. Clerks copied messages between notes and mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing routing and form features cover the core changes. Small connectors can now be built and maintained more cheaply.
tasks.still_hard: Call purpose can be ambiguous. Distressed callers, confidential requests and absent recipients need human handling.
tasks.human_edge: Put callers at ease, recognise urgency and avoid disclosing information to the wrong person.

ambition.what: An acknowledged callback queue for callers who cannot reach a recipient.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and forwarding notes, and more time resolving difficult routing. They gain discretion to prioritise callbacks within agreed limits.

reach.task: Coordinate callbacks and cover arrangements for unavailable colleagues.
reach.learn: Availability rules, escalation paths and clear message writing.

evidence.claim: Directories, transfer rules, structured message forms and notifications can be configured without a model.
Keeping caller confirmation avoids relying on unverified speech transcription for names and numbers.

assumptions: Step shares average transferred calls and message-taking calls; each caller does not follow both branches.
The clerk remains the main telephone contact.
The design does not require call recording or speech transcription.
Directory and message handling offer clearer gains than automating the human conversation.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which routing and form features are already licensed?
Who maintains recipient and cover information?
Which calls need identity checks or immediate escalation?
Which availability fields may the clerk access?
Do national rules require employee consultation?
research_questions: Where do failed transfers and missed callbacks arise?
Can existing configuration provide the complete message workflow?
new_work: Handle failed notifications and overdue callbacks.
Review access and retention for personal contact details under GDPR.
Check the EU AI Act implications if speech processing is added later.

tasks.short: Answer questions, explain information, record orders and help resolve complaints.

steps.what: Listen to the person and clarify their question, order or complaint.
Find approved information and relevant account, order or case records.
Write a response using the retrieved information.

loop.input: Clarified free-text request and access-filtered response facts with source references.
loop.output: Response draft with cited facts and explicit unanswered questions.
loop.check: Check source references, amounts and identifiers against retrieved records; the clerk checks meaning and tone.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one revision per request; missing sources or failed checks return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use templates for standard questions. Varied wording and explanations need a bounded drafting loop.

steps.what: Explain the answer, respond to follow-up questions and check understanding.
Enter order details and confirm the customer's instructions.
Send the accepted order confirmation.
Discuss the complaint and propose a remedy or escalation.
Approve a remedy outside the clerk's delegated limits.
Send the complaint outcome and update the case.

tasks.design: An access-controlled answer desk joins approved material in the {DOCS} with permitted records from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {HELPDESK}. Templates answer standard questions; one bounded loop drafts varied explanations for clerk review, while configured order forms and outcome templates handle paperwork. People retain the conversation and approve orders, exceptional remedies and complaint notices at their action points.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding current facts required several searches. Unstructured questions did not fit fixed templates, and complaints needed personal judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors and template generators are cheaper to build with AI-assisted coding. Bounded drafting can use retrieved facts without granting independent decision authority.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting policies, identity checks and contractual promises need care. A fluent draft can still misstate what the company may offer.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the person needs, explain limits respectfully and repair trust after a failure.

ambition.what: A daily review of recurring complaint causes with the service manager.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and composing routine paperwork, leaving more time for explanation and complaint follow-up. They can recommend service changes; remedy limits require explicit delegation.

reach.task: Identify recurring inquiry and complaint causes.
reach.learn: Consistent case coding, process mapping and separating patterns from isolated incidents.

reach.task: Improve escalation and delegated remedy procedures.
reach.learn: Service policy, approval thresholds and complaint review.

evidence.claim: Record lookup, order forms and confirmation templates can use deterministic technology.
Source-grounded drafting can assist varied explanations while people retain consequential decisions.
GDPR and EU AI Act obligations depend on data processing and intended use; these are not automatically employment decisions.

assumptions: The steps cover question, order and complaint branches; not every request follows all branches.
The step involving the service manager includes approval time within the end-to-end task.
Routine orders are within the clerk's delegated authority.
An accepted order can trigger a fixed confirmation without a second approval.
The assistant cannot grant remedies, change policy or send free-text drafts independently.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which policies are authoritative and who updates them?
What order and remedy authority does the clerk have?
Which systems permit record lookup and validated writes?
What identity checks apply to customer and employee inquiries?
Which GDPR requirements and national consultation rules apply to the proposed processing?
research_questions: Which inquiry types fit templates without a model?
Can draft checks detect unsupported promises and incorrect record references?
Does the intended use introduce an EU AI Act high-risk use case?
new_work: Review varied drafts and handle missing or conflicting sources.
Maintain policy versions, templates and escalation limits.
Test factual accuracy and recipient access.
Review recurring complaint causes with the service manager.
Maintain GDPR retention and access controls and assess EU AI Act requirements for the actual use.

tasks.short: Keep filing, stock, mailing and database records accurate and current.

steps.what: Collect record changes and supporting documents from colleagues.
Check identifiers, required fields, duplicates and supporting evidence.
Update document indexes, names, folders and filing metadata.
Enter office stock receipts, issues and location changes.
Update addresses, contact details and mailing preferences.
Copy updates into a shared tracker for cross-team reconciliation.
Count physical office stock and compare it with recorded quantities.
Investigate discrepancies and propose corrections.
Approve restricted corrections and record dispositions.
File retained paper and carry out approved physical archive changes.

tasks.design: Use structured change forms in the {WORKFLOW}, existing record controls in the {DOCS} and {CRM}, and validated stock-event integration with the {ERP}. A shared exception queue replaces the copied {SPREADSHEET} tracker, while approved corrections return to the same validated update path. People investigate discrepancies, approve restricted changes and handle physical stock and archives.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived without stable identifiers or complete evidence. Separate teams maintained duplicate trackers and different validation rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms and record controls already cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of small connectors, validation and reconciliation views.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence cannot be created by software. Physical counts, conflicting ownership and historical duplicates need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Find the real cause of a discrepancy and distinguish a genuine change from a mistaken or unauthorised request.

ambition.what: A weekly office-stock replenishment recommendation based on verified consumption.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time checking discrepancies and recommending replenishment, with less re-keying. They can recommend stock levels; purchasing and restricted record decisions remain with authorised roles.

reach.task: Reconcile stock movements and explain count differences.
reach.learn: Stock-event identifiers, count procedures and adjustment controls.

reach.task: Improve document indexing and retention accuracy.
reach.learn: Metadata standards, retention schedules and access classification.

evidence.claim: Structured forms, validation and record integrations can replace repeated entry without model interpretation.
A documented spreadsheet row-limit failure lost public-health records, supporting explicit completeness checks.

assumptions: The company uses the {DOCS}, {ERP} and {CRM} for the represented record types.
A shared {SPREADSHEET} tracker bridges teams despite structured source records.
These are branches of a recurring maintenance cycle, not mandatory steps for every change.
Automatic writes are limited to authorised, validated routine changes; restricted changes enter the approval queue.
The records owner is the relevant owner for each record type.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which system is authoritative for each record type?
Are stable identifiers and supported write interfaces available?
Which tracker fields duplicate source records?
Which changes require approval, including deletion and mailing permissions?
What paper retention and national consultation rules apply?
How often do physical counts and restricted approvals occur?
research_questions: Can structured intake remove most missing-field exceptions?
Which existing record controls can replace custom code?
Can reconciliation detect missing, duplicate and partially applied changes?
new_work: Investigate rejected changes and reconciliation differences.
Maintain field mappings, validation rules and access permissions.
Check import completeness and retry failures without creating duplicates.
Keep retention and mailing-preference controls current under GDPR.
Assess EU AI Act requirements if model interpretation is later introduced.

role.altitude: The office clerk becomes a stronger coordinator of document quality, caller follow-up and record accuracy. Routine handling shrinks; broader spending, remedy or retention authority requires explicit delegation.
reach: File clerk: document indexing, accessible packs and retention accuracy.
Administrative assistant: callbacks, cover arrangements and escalation.
Inventory clerk: stock reconciliation and replenishment recommendations.
Management analyst: recurring inquiry and complaint causes.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, routing and document templates.
Review source-grounded drafts and spot unsupported claims.
Handle difficult conversations and explain service limits.
Apply access, retention and approval rules.
role.ambitious_version: Run an office support improvement service that turns verified stock use, failed callbacks and recurring complaints into specific proposals for the administrative services manager.
